I feel like I do a decent job at cutting my fabric but I'd like to get better at it, any guides or tips would be greatly appreciated.
Anyone have a good guide on cutting fabric?

1. Always Iron your fabric if possible. Some fabric distort if you glide with the iron and you may need to press downwards. It can be time consuming especially if you have a lot of yardage but it makes a difference.

  2. Completely flatten the fabric and match the selvages. You can use a yard stick to help pull the whole thing straight.

  3. Use a proper cutting implement and make sure its sharp.

  4. Do not lift up the fabric as you cut or pin. Some fabrics are heavy enough to stay in place other need to be weighted down. Learn to pin without lifting the fabric. Takes some practice. You may need to use one hand to keep the fabric flat while you cut with the other as well. This greatly increases accuracy.

  5. Instead of struggling to cut awkward corners, rotate your fabric in place. You may need to cut your project into smaller sections and then trim them down.

Got any specific questions?

Thanks! The problem I struggle with most is cutting straight, even with a chalk outline to cut, it seems like I'll not have cut a straight line, though maybe the problem is also that I made the pattern from old clothing.

Troubleshoot your cutting. I would start with getting your tools sharpened. Dull tools will pull and pucker fabric as they cut.

If you do a lot of cutting, make the investment in a pair of knife edge shears if you don't already have them and learn to sharpen and oil them. Expect to spend $30-$50 on a 7-9 inch pair.

Lay the top blade of the scissors directly onto the line so that you see exactly what is about to be cut before it happens. If you're using your left hand to cut, get left-handed scissors ("ambidextrous" scissors do not exist).

Using scissors this way is as good as having a laser guide.
My most common methods are a razor roller and a giant heavy pair of metal scissors.

This is what I use. I picked mine up from Joann Fabric.

http://demandware.edgesuite.net/aamm_prd/on/demandware.static/-/Sites-joann-product-catalog/default/dwbd43ed0e/images/hi-res/alt/2517431ALT1.jpg
Is that pretty easy to learn to use?

I use a pair of these spring-loaded Fiskars to cut most of my fabric. I have a big warning written on them "FOR FABRIC ONLY" to prevent anyone from ruining them with paper or worse. I've had my pair for 10 years now, and they're still going strong and sharp. They cut cleanly all the way down to the tip of the scissors, which I think is very important to get crisp corners and curves. They are spring-loaded, so cutting doesn't make the hands ache; I could cut fabric all day. The bottom blade of the scissors can rest nearly flat on the table surface, so you're really just squeezing the top blade down, which increases accuracy in cutting. Highly recommend.

I have a pair of these smaller spring-loaded Fiskars that I use mostly to cut smaller things out of fabric: notches and things like that.

For cutting quilt blocks, rectangles for bags and straps, squaring up fabric, bias tape, and more, I use an Olfa rotary cutter, a self-healing mat, and an Olipfa ruler. The Olipfa ruler is nice, because the bottom edge can be butted up to the edge of the rotary mat for an accurate 90 degree angle. Very accurate. Nice to have.
